description_en: The Dakṣiṇakālī Temple is situated in the south-western quadrant of the Kathmandu Valley, to the south of the ancient settlement of Pharping, within a forested area. The temple, revered as the lineage deity of the Śāha kings of Nepal and the Rāṇā rulers, is among the most powerful and renownedśaktipīṭhas of the country which The surrounding locality itself came to be known as Dakṣiṇakālī after the temple. The shrine is established near the confluence (dobhāna) of the Uddhāravatī and Pūrnāvatī streams, close to a cremation ground (śmaśānaghāṭa). At thepīṭha, the principal image of the goddess Kālī is installed facing east. She is identified as a deity of the southernāmnāya(K. Koirālā, VS 2065, p. 60). The image of Dakṣiṇakālī is depicted in a relatively gentle (saumya) form. To the south of the main image are installed the Aṣṭamātṛkās—Brahmāyaṇī, Māheśvarī, Kaumārī, Vaiṣṇavī, Vārāhī, and Indrāyaṇī—together with Gaṇeśa. Directly in front of the main image stand Bhairava and three metal bells. Within thepīṭhaprecinct, an image of Cāmuṇḍā—regarded as one of the forms of Dakṣiṇakālī—is also present near the goddess. During sacrificial rites (balī), blood offerings are obligatorily presented to Cāmuṇḍā, Vārāhī, and Narasiṃhī. Dakṣiṇakālī has long been venerated by the Śāha kings and the Rāṇā family as their lineage deity (kuladevī).According to local oral tradition, the Dakṣiṇakālī Pīṭha was originally located on a high hillock above the temple of Śikhara­nārāyaṇa. As the settlement below became insecure, contemporary tantric practitioners are believed to have compelled the goddess, through the power of mantras, to relocate with her attendant deities to a dwelling place at the river confluence and cremation ground below Pharping. Remains found on the hill are said to corroborate this relocation of thepīṭha(Ṭ. Śreṣṭha, VS 2078, p. 70).According to theDevamālā Vaṃśāvalī(Y. Naraharinātha, VS 2013, p. 62), only thepīṭhaoriginally existed here. The goddess is said to have appeared in the dream of King Pratāpa Malla and instructed him to create and install her image. The first image commissioned by the king was fierce and unmanifest, prompting the goddess to reappear in his dream and direct that it be installed within the palace instead. With the assistance of his guru Lambakarṇa Bhaṭṭa, Pratāpa Malla then installed a second image at thepīṭha. TheBhāṣā Vaṃśāvalīprovides further detail, stating that Pratāpa Malla completed the consecration rites by performingmahāpūjā,sahasrabalī, andnarabalī, and formally installed the image on the day of Vaiśākha Śukla Tṛtīyā (D. Laṃsāla, VS 2023, pp. 82–83).The earliest known inscription related to Dakṣiṇakālī dates to NS 360 (VS 1297) and is found on the crown of the image used in the Hariśaṅkara Jātrā. Local belief maintains that Dakṣiṇakālī was also known as Kankeśvarī, theśaktiof Kanakeśvara Śiva (K. Koirālā, VS 2065, p. 66), suggesting that the goddess may earlier have been known by this name. After the unification of Nepal, the Śāha kings instituted the worship and festivals of Dakṣiṇakālī of Pharping, located closer to the Valley, in place of the Kālīkā of Gorkhā (Ṭ. Śreṣṭha, VS 2078, p. 72). King Girvāṇayuddha Vikrama Śāha endowed 504murī(approximately 126ropanī) of land in 1799 CE (VS 1856) asguṭhīfor the performance of daily worship andmahāpūjā(thāpūjā) (Ṭ. Śreṣṭha, VS 2078, pp. 182–183).Offerings,guṭhīarrangements, and inscriptions donated over different periods by kings, nobles, local officials, and lay patrons testify to the historical prosperity of the Dakṣiṇakālī temple. Rulers and high dignitaries before and after Pratāpa Malla expressed their devotion by offering metal images, silver and gold ornaments, drums (nagarā),kikiṃpā, crowns, and other valuables. During the reign of Girvāṇayuddha Vikrama Śāha, aguṭhīof 504murīof land was formally established in 1799 CE (VS 1856) for the goddess’s daily worship andmahāpūjā(D. Vajrācārya & Ṭ. Śreṣṭha, VS 2078, pp. 301–303; K. Koirālā, VS 2065, p. 66). In 1802 CE (VS 1859), a donor named Lakṣmī offered anagarāand established aguṭhīto ensure its use during daily worship. An inscription preserved in the collection of Gaṇeślāl Mānandhara of Pharping records that in 1848 CE (VS 1905), Surendra Vikrama Śāha donated a silver crown and ornaments and established akheṭaguṭhīfor the goddess. In the same year, Bhavanakumārī, the wife of Kāji Amṛtasiṃha Thāpā, offered a gildedkikiṃpā, a crown, and 108tolāof silver. In 1849 CE (VS 1906), General Amarasiṃha Thāpā is likewise recorded as having made offerings to Dakṣiṇakālī. Around 1884 CE (VS 1941), the younger queen of Jītejaṅga Bahādur Rāṇā performedpañcabalīworship and offered garments to the goddess. In 1900 CE (VS 1957), Vīra Śamśer Rāṇā constructed apāṭīand dedicated it to the deity, and in 1917 CE (VS 1974), Pṛthvī Vīra Vikrama Śāha and the junior queen donated the bell located on the right side of the shrine. In 1922 CE (VS 1979), Chibdhoja Śāha, the eldest son of Raṇśer Śāha and grandson of Prāṇa Śāha, offered a gildedcaduvāadorned with four nāgas and tassels, and endowed akheṭaguṭhīfor the annualVarṣabandhanarite performed on Jyeṣṭha Śukla Daśamī. An inscription behind the temple records that in 1960 CE (VS 2017), on the occasion of King Mahendra Vīra Vikrama Śāha’s birthday, the embankments, walls, and surroundingpāṭī–sattalastructures were restored. More recently, in 2016 CE (VS 2073), Dal Bahādur Deuwā and his family of Dhangadhī constructed and dedicated the temple’s entrance gateway, as recorded on an inscription affixed to the gateway wall.Dakṣiṇakālī is worshipped as a goddess who grants royal power and victory over enemies. The temple priests are Karmācāryas, who conduct the daily worship and all ritual observances according to tantric procedures. In addition to the priests, members of the Maharjan and Poḍe communities play significant roles in temple operations. The Maharjans are responsible for animal sacrifice, managing ritual vessels and ornaments, registering donated goods with the Guṭhī Saṃsthān, and safeguarding them. The Poḍes undertake cleaning of the temple परिसर, handle offerings such as clothing, adornments, and fruits, slaughter sacrificial animals—buffaloes, goats, sheep, ducks, and chickens—and release pigeons. For the security of the shrine, four Maharjans and four Poḍes are customarily assigned (Ṭ. Śreṣṭha, VS 2078, p. 101).Major ritual observances includemahāpūjā(thāpūjā) performed annually on Vaiśākha Kṛṣṇa Trayodaśī and Bhādra Kṛṣṇa Aṣṭamī (K. Koirālā, VS 2065, p. 66). The historic Hariśaṅkara Jātrā of Pharping, held from Bhādra Śukla Caturdaśī to Āśvina Kṛṣṇa Caturdaśī, incorporates the palanquin (khaṭa) of Dakṣiṇakālī, with a special procession on the night of Āśvina Kṛṣṇa Daśamī. During this festival, residents of Tipī Tol carry the palanquin of Dakṣiṇakālī from Thalkhu Tol through Kochhu Tol, Yalkhu Tol, and back to Thalkhu Tol. The Dakṣiṇakālīdyaḥchẽ(PRN0130) is located in Tipī Tol. Among the four annual Navarātrīs, Baḍā Daśaiṃ (ninth of bright fortnight of the month of Āśvina) and Cāite Daśaiṃ (ninth of bright fortnight of the month of Caitra) are observed here as major festivals of Bhagavatī, marked by worship and animal sacrifice (K. Koirālā, VS 2065, p. 66). In addition, every Saturday and Tuesday, large numbers of devotees gather at the temple fordarśanaand worship of the goddess.
description_ne: नेपालका शाह राजाहरू र राणा शासकहरूको इष्टदेवी मानिने दक्षिणकाली माता अवस्थित यो मन्दिर नेपालको प्रसिद्ध र शक्तिशाली पीठहरू मध्ये एक हो । यहाँ राजा प्रताप मल्लले दक्षिणकाली देवीको मूर्ति स्थापना गरेको थियो ।दक्षिणकाली शक्तिपीठ काठमाडौ उपत्यकाको नैऋत्य-कोणतिर (दक्षिण-पश्चिम दिशा) मा अवस्थित छ । यो नेपालको प्राचीन बस्ती फर्पिङको दक्षिणतिर जङ्गलमा रहेको छ । यो नेपालको शक्तिशाली र प्रसिद्ध पीठहरूमध्ये पर्दछ । यस मन्दिरको नामबाट नै यस क्षेत्रको नाम दक्षिणकाली रहन गएको छ । जङ्गलबाट बग्दै आएका दुई खोला उद्धारवती तथा पूर्णावतीको दोभान र समसानघाट नजिक पीठ स्थापित छ । पीठमा प्रमुख देवीको रूपमा कालीको मूर्ति पूर्वाभिमुख गरी स्थापना गरिएको छ । यी देवी दक्षिण आम्नायकी देवी हुन् (K. Koirālā VS 2065, p. 60) । यहाँ स्थापित दक्षिणकालीको मूर्ति सौम्य रूपको रहेको छ । दक्षिणकाली मूर्तिको दक्षिणपट्टि अष्टमातृका (ब्रह्मायणी, माहेश्वरी, कौमारी, वैष्णवी, वाराही, इन्द्रायणी) का साथै गणेशको मूर्ति स्थापना गरेिएको छ । त्यसैगरी मूल मूर्तिको ठीक अगाडि भैरव र धातुको तीनवटा घण्टा पनि देख्न सकिन्छ । दक्षिणकाली पीठमा देवीको नजिक चामुण्डाको मूर्ति पर्छ, जो दक्षिणकालीकै एक रूप हो । दक्षिणकालीमा बलि चढाउँदा चामुण्डा, वाराही र नरसिंहीलाई अनिवार्य रूपमा बलिको रक्त अर्पण गरिन्छ । दक्षिणकालीलाई नेपालको शाह राजा र राणा परिवारले इष्टदेवी (कुलदेवी) का रूपमा मान्ने गर्दछन् ।स्थानीय जनविश्वास (अनुश्रुति) अनुसार, दक्षिणकाली पीठ पहिले शिखरनारायणको मन्दिरभन्दा माथिको अग्लो थुम्कामा थियो । बस्तीका मानिस असुरक्षित भएपछि तत्कालीन तान्त्रिकाचार्यहरूले मन्त्रबलद्वारा देवीलाई आफ्ना गणसहित फर्पिङ सहरभन्दा तल खोलाको दोभान र समसानघाटमा आवासभूमि बनाउन बाध्य पारेका थिए । उक्त डाँडामा रहेका अवशेष चिह्नले पनि पीठ सारिएको कुराको पुष्टि गर्दछ (Ṭ. Śreṣṭha VS 2078, p. 70)।देवमाला वंशावली (Y. Naraharinātha VS 2013 p. 62) अनुसार यहाँ पीठ मात्र स्थापित थियो । राजा प्रताप मल्लको सपनामा देवी आई आफ्नो मूर्ति बनाई स्थापना गर्नु भनी आज्ञा भए अनुसार राजाले मूर्ति बनाई स्थापना गरेका थिए । राजाले बनाउन लगाएको पहिलो मूर्ति अप्रकाशित र उग्रमूर्ति भएकोले देवीबाट पुन: सपनामा आई दरबारमा स्थापना गर्नु भनेका थिए भने दोस्रो मूर्तिलाई गुरू लम्बकर्ण भट्टको सहयोहले पीठमा स्थापना गरेका हुन् । भाषा वंशावली अनुसार यस घटनाको थप विवरण दिँदै, प्रताप मल्लले ‘महापूजा, सहस्रबलि र नरबलि’ सम्पन्न गरी प्रतिष्ठाकर्मको विधि पुऱ्याई वैशाख शुक्ल तृतीयाका दिन मूर्ति स्थापना गराएको कुरा उल्लेख गरेको छ ( D. Laṃsāla VS 2023, pp. 82-83)दक्षिणकाली सम्बन्धी सबैभन्दा पुरानो अभिलेख नेसं. ३६० (विसं १२९७) को हरिशङ्कर जात्रामा प्रयोग गरिने मूर्तिको मुकुटमा भेटिएको छ । स्थानीय मान्यता अनुसार कनकेश्वर शिवकी शक्ति दक्षिणकाली, कनकेश्वरी नाउँले पनि प्रसिद्ध रहिछन् भन्ने थाहा हुन्छ (K. Koirālā VS 2065, p. 66) । यस आधारमा दक्षिणकालीलाई पहिले कनकेश्वरी भनिन्थ्यो होला भन्ने अनुमान गरिएको छ । नेपालको एकीकरणपछि शाह राजाहरूले गोर्खाकी कालिकाको सट्टा उपत्यका नजिकको फर्पिङको दक्षिणकालीको पूजा-पर्व चलाउने व्यवस्था मिलाए (Ṭ. Śreṣṭha VS 2078, p. 72)। राजा गीर्वाणयुद्धविक्रम शाहले विसं १८५६ (सन् १७९९) मा दैनिक र महापूजा (थापूजा) चलाउनका लागि ५०४ मुरी (१२६ रोपनी) गुठी जग्गा सङ्कल्प गरी राखेका थिए (Ṭ. Śreṣṭha VS 2078, pp. 182-183)दक्षिणकाली मन्दिरमा विभिन्न कालखण्डमा राजादेखि सामन्त, जिम्मावाल तथा स्थानीय दाताहरूले चढाएको मौलिक चढावा, गुठी व्यवस्था तथा अभिलेखहरू मन्दिरको ऐतिहासिक समृद्धिको महत्वपूर्ण प्रमाण हुन् । प्रताप मल्लका पूर्व–पश्चात् शासक तथा उच्च पदस्थ व्यक्तिहरूले देवीप्रति आफ्नो आस्था प्रकट गर्दै अनेकौं धातुका मूर्ति, रजत–स्वर्णाभूषण, नगरा, किकिंपा, मुकुट तथा अन्य चढावाहरू अर्पण गरेका छन् । श्री ५ गीर्वाणयुद्ध विक्रम शाहको पालामा विसं १८५६ (सन् १७९९) मा दक्षिणकालीका नित्यपूजा र महापूजाका लागि ५०४ मुरी जग्गा सङ्कल्प गरी गुठी स्थापना गरिएको उल्लेख  छ (D. Vajrācārya & Ṭ. Śreṣṭha VS 2078, pp. 301–303,  K. Koirālā VS 2065, p. 66) । त्यसैगरी विसं १८५९ (सन् १८०२) मा लक्ष्मी नाम गरेको व्यक्तिले देवीलाई नगरा चढाई नित्यपूजाका क्रममा बजाउनुपर्ने व्यवस्था मिलाउँदै गुठी स्थापना गराएकी थिइन् । फर्पिङका जिम्मावाल गणेशलाल मानन्धरको संग्रहमा रहेको अभिलेखअनुसार विसं १९०५ (सन् १८४८) मा सुरेन्द्र विक्रम शाहले दक्षिणकालीलाई चाँदीको मुकुट र गहना चढाई खेटगुठी राखिदिएका थिए । सोही वर्ष काजी अमृतसिंह थापाकी पत्नी भवनकुमारीले सुनकाको मोलम्बा गरिएको किकिंपा, मुकुट र १०८ तोला चाँदी अर्पण गरेको थियो । त्यसपछि विसं १९०६ (सन् १८४९) मा श्री ३ इष्टदेवता दक्षिणकाली मातालाई जनरल अमरसिंह थापाद्वारा चढावाको उल्लेख अभिलेखमा भेटिन्छ । विसं १९४१ (सन् १८८४) तिर जीतजङ्गबहादुर राणाकी काहिला रानीले पंचबली पूजा गरी देवीलाई पोशाक चढाएको उल्लेख छ । विसं १९५७ (सन् १९००) मा वीर शमशेर राणाद्वारा पाटी निर्माण गरी देवीलाई अर्पण गरिएको तथा विसं १९७४ (सन् १९१७) मा पृथ्वी वीर विक्रम शाह र साहिला बडामहारानीले दाहिनेपट्टि रहेको घण्टा चढाएको अभिलेखमा उल्लेख छ । त्यसपछि विसं १९७९ (सन् १९२२) मा प्राण साहाका नाति रणशेर साहाका जेठा छोरा चिभधोज साहाले सुनको मोलम्बा भएको चार नागसहितको चदुवा र झल्लर चढाई ज्येष्ठ शुक्ल दशमीका दिन हुने वर्षबन्धन पूजाका लागि खेतगुठी राखिदिए । साथै विसं २०१७ (सन् १९६०) मा महेन्द्र वीरविक्रम शाहको जन्मजयन्तीको अवसरमा मन्दिर वरपरका बाँध, पर्खाल तथा पाटी–सत्तलहरूको जीर्णोद्धार गरिएको विवरण मन्दिर पछाडिको  अभिलेखमा रहेको छ । पछिल्लोसमय धनगढी बस्ने दल बहादुर देउवा र परिवारले  विसं २०७३ (सन् २०१६) मन्दिर प्रबेशद्वार निर्माण गरी मातालाई समर्पित गरेको अभिलेख द्वारको पर्खालका टाँसिएको छ ।दक्षिणकालीलाई राज्य-ऐश्वर्यप्राप्ति र शत्रुविजयका लागि पूजा गरिने देवी मानिन्छ । यहाँको पुजारी कर्माचार्यहरू हुने गर्दछन् । पुजारीले यहाँको नित्यपूजा लगायत सम्पूर्ण पूजापाठहरू संचालन गर्ने कार्य गर्दछन् । यहाँ तान्त्रिक विधिबाट देवको पूजा गर्ने प्रचलन गरेको छ । पुजारी बाहेक महर्जन र पोडे थरका समुदायहरूको पनि मन्दिरमा महत्वपुर्ण भूमिका रहन्छ । महर्जनहरूको प्रमुख काम पशुबलि दिने, भाँडाकुँडा, गरगहना जिम्मा लिने, देवस्थलमा चढाइएका जिन्सी सामान गुठी संस्थानमा दर्ता गरी आफ्नो जिम्मा लिई राख्ने आदि हो । त्यसैगरी पोडेहरूले मन्दिर परिसर सरसफाई गर्ने, चढाइएका सामग्रीहरूमा कपडा, शृङ्गारका सामान, फलफूल जिम्मा लिने तथा बलिका लागि ल्याइएका राँगा, बोका, थुमा, हाँस, कखुरा काट्ने र परेवा उडाउने काम रहेका छन् । साथै देवस्थलको सुरक्षार्थ चार जना महर्जन र चारजना पोडेलाई खटाइने व्यवस्था रहेको हुन्छ (Ṭ. Śreṣṭha VS 2078, p 101)।यसको साथै प्रत्येक वर्षको वैशाखकृष्ण त्रयोदशी र भाद्र कृष्ण अष्टमीमा यहाँ महापूजा (थापूजा) गरिने परम्परा छ (K. Koirālā VS 2065, p. 66)। फर्पिङमा भाद्र शुक्ल चतुर्दशीदेखी सुरू भई आश्विनकृष्ण चतुर्दशीसम्म मनाइने ऐतिहासिक हरिशङ्करजात्रामा दक्षिणकालीको खट सम्मिलित गर्ने चलन रहेको छ । विशेषगरी आश्विन कृष्ण दशमीको राति दक्षिणकालीको खटयात्रा गरिन्छ । यस जात्रामा, टिपीटोलका व्यक्तिहरूले दक्षिणकालीको खट थलखुटोलबाट बोकी कोछुटोल, यलखुटोल, थलखुटोल घुमाई थलखुटोलमा राख्छन् । टिपी टोलमा दक्षिणकालीको द्य:छेँ (PRN0130) रहेको छ । वर्षको चार नवरात्रीमध्ये बडादसैँ (आश्विन शुक्ल नवमी) र चैतेदसैँ (चैत्रशुक्ल नवमी) मा यहाँ भगवतीको विशेष पर्व मानी पूजाआजा पशु बलि दिने गरिन्छ (K. Koirālā VS 2065 , p. 66) । यसबाहेक हरेक हप्ता शनिबार र मंगलबार यहाँ श्रद्धालु भक्तजनको देवी दर्शन र पूजा प्रार्थनाको लागि भीड लाग्ने गर्दछ ।

historical_events.event_description: According to tradition, the goddess appeared to King Pratāpa Malla in a dream and commanded him to fashion and install her image; in obedience to this injunction, the king had the image made and consecrated. TheBhāṣā Vaṃśāvalīprovides further details of this event, stating that Pratāpa Malla performed the full rites of consecration (pratiṣṭhākarman) by completing themahāpūjā,sahasrabali, andnarabali, and formally installed the image on third of bright fortnight of Vaiśākha.
During the reign of Girvāṇayuddha Vikrama Śāha, aguṭhīendowment of 504murīof land was established to support the daily worship (nityapūjā) and themahāpūjāof Dakṣiṇakālī.
Lakṣmī Damāī donated a ceremonial drum (nagarā) to Dakṣiṇakālī Māta and instituted aguṭhīto ensure that thenagarāwould be played regularly during the daily morning and evening worship.

historical_events.event_name: Offering a silver crown and ornaments
historical_events.event_description: According to an inscription preserved in the collection of Śrī Gaṇeślāla Mānandhara, ajimmāvālaof Pharping, Surendra Vikrama Śāha offered a silver crown and ornaments to Dakṣiṇakālī and endowed agriculturalguṭhīland to ensure the annual performance of worship.

historical_events.event_name: Offering of gilded caduvā, kikiṃpā, crown, and silver
historical_events.event_description: Among the series of stone inscriptions erected behind the Dakṣiṇakālī Temple, one records that Śrī Bhuvanakumārī, the wife of Kāji Amṛtasiṃha Thāpā, donated to the goddess a gildedcaduvā(ilāṃ), akikiṃpā, a crown, and 108tolāof silver.

An inscription is engraved around the gildedcaduvāof the Dakṣiṇakālī Temple. Although the text is no longer fully legible, the surviving portions indicate that thecaduvā(ilāṃ) was offered to the goddess by General Amṛtasiṃha Thāpā.

According to details contained in a letter sent to General Jītajaṅga Bahādura Rāṇā, the Kāhilā Rānī organized apañcabalisacrifice and requested that the necessary ritual materials be dispatched. The letter further instructs that, after the completion of the ritual, an account be kept of the garments offered to the goddess and that the sacrificial buffalo be distributed among the localdvāreandpradhāna.
Vīra Śamaśera Rāṇā constructed apāṭīwithin the Dakṣiṇakālī Temple complex and dedicated it to the goddess.
Pṛthvī Vīravikrama Śāha and the Sāhilā Baḍāmahārānī Dharmśīlavatī offered a bell to the goddess.

Acting upon a vow (saṅkalpa) made by Cautariyā Chibhadhoja Śāha, Cautāriyā Jaṅgapratāpa Śāha, together with his family, offered to the goddess a gildedcaduvāadorned with fournāgafigures. To ensure the preservation of the nāga images and the uninterrupted continuation of worship, aguṭhīwas established to cover maintenance and ritual expenses.

historical_events.event_name: Renovation of pāṭī and sattala structures
historical_events.event_description: On the occasion of the birth anniversary of King Mahendra, embankments and boundary walls within the temple precinct were constructed in his name, and the surroundingpāṭīandsattalastructures were renovated. This information is recorded in one of the inscriptions erected behind the Dakṣiṇakālī Temple.

An inscription affixed to the wall of the temple gateway records that Dala Bahādura Deuvā of Dhangadhi and his family constructed and dedicated the temple entrance gate to the goddess in 2016 CE (VS 2073).
